A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching experiments relocated in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original LASSO and Lotka–Volterra simulations, bag-count sensitivity experiments and a supplementary regression case study.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds original graphical-LASSO stability results on a flow-cytometry dataset.

M1.justification: The bagging-then-inflated-argmax procedure and its geometric selection rule remain unchanged. Graphical LASSO supplies another base learner for the existing framework. Removing Algorithm 2 changes implementation documentation, not the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds graph-structure selection on real flow-cytometry measurements of 11 proteins across 759 cells (Section 5.2). This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained synthetic regression and dynamical-system tasks. The larger regression example remains in Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the same selection pipelines: unbagged argmax, bagged argmax, top-k, inclusion-probability thresholding and the proposed inflated argmax. V2 applies this comparator set with graphical LASSO as the shared base learner for the added graph task; membership in the retained comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new graph experiment introduces 759 leave-one-out evaluations, bags of 700 samples, five-fold selection of lambda, and average LOO set size. Epsilon is chosen to match top-2 instability, while tau matches graph sparsity. The earlier experiments retain their settings and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: V2 adds a graph case study comparing the two most frequently selected structures and identifying their single differing edge (Figure 5). The existing bag-count sensitivity tests and larger regression case study are retained, with unchanged experimental plots.

E5.justification: The 200 regression trials, 100 Lotka–Volterra trials and empirical-CDF reporting are retained. V2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests or new repeated-run reporting practice. Its graph experiment uses one dataset and reports LOO outcomes.

E6.justification: V2 adds a complete graph-selection comparison. Table 2 reports instability of 0.453 for unbagged argmax, 0.112 for bagged argmax, 0.013 for inclusion-probability selection, and 0.008 for both top-2 and inflated argmax; their latter set sizes are 2.00 and 1.58. Earlier experimental plots and STRidge validation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The central stability bound, geometric inflated-argmax definition and appendix epsilon calculation remain unchanged. V2 omits v1's explicit general black-box-to-weight construction in Equation (2), while adding the Gaussian precision-matrix assumptions and graphical-LASSO formulation. These are limited formal changes; no new stability theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: V2 expands the abstract's empirical contribution to graph selection and explicitly claims the first model-selection stability guarantee agnostic to models, base algorithm and data distribution. The central contribution of stabilizing black-box selection through bagging and inflated argmax remains intact.

C2.justification: V2 interprets near-tied graph frequencies as uncertainty and identifies the pakts473–pmek connection as a target for follow-up experiments. It also states that epsilon is determined by a requested stability tolerance rather than tuned, although the graph experiment selects it empirically. Earlier LOO-scope and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the flow-cytometry dataset identifier, graph bagging parameters and lambda search over 1–500, selecting 77 (Appendix D.2). Conversely, it removes v1's explicit inflated-argmax computational recipe in Algorithm 2. Existing regression and SINDy implementation details are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hewitt (1921), Sachs et al. (2005), and Soloff et al.'s Bagging provides assumption-free stability. It makes the classification-to-model-selection positioning and priority claim more explicit. The existing inflated-argmax reference is retained with updated publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and reorganizes background, conventional selection rules, stability and the proposed approach. Regression exposition and results move into Appendices A–C, SINDy background is integrated into its experiment, and experimental details receive a new subsection structure.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the three-panel appendix argmax illustration with an annotated main-text diagram, separates v1 Figure 2 into Figures 3 and 7, and relocates numerous displays. It adds graph correlation and structure figures, a validation curve and a results table, and reformats existing tables.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful real-data evidence beyond v1's simulations: Table 2 demonstrates equal instability to top-2 with fewer returned graphs. The reorganized exposition also clarifies the framework's connection to classification. These gains are limited by the single graph dataset and absence of graph-accuracy validation. Removing Algorithm 2 and introducing inconsistent guidance about epsilon selection partly offset the improvement.
